timeline.title: Military Aviation Timeline | Vol d'Histoire
timeline.hero_desc: 75 years of strategic innovation. From the first Cold War jets to 5th generation stealth fighters — explore every decade.
timeline.empty_desc: No aircraft matches the active filters
timeline.era_1940_desc: The era of the first military jet engines, transitioning from propellers.
timeline.era_1950_desc: The supersonic arms race, rise of the East-West blocs.
timeline.era_1960_desc: Mach 2+, guided missiles — dogfight doctrine evolves radically.
timeline.era_1970_desc: First 3rd generation fighters with pulse-Doppler radar and digital avionics.
timeline.era_1980_desc: Digital avionics, fly-by-wire, BVR missiles — warfare goes electronic.
timeline.era_1990_desc: Transition to asymmetric conflicts, maturity of the 4th generation.
timeline.era_2000_desc: 5th generation — data fusion, active stealth, supercruise.
timeline.era_2010_desc: Network integration, onboard AI — towards the 6th generation.
timeline.era_2020_desc: Autonomous systems, combat drones, human-machine hybridization.
timeline.hero_desc_full: 75 years of strategic innovation. From the first Cold War jets to 5th generation stealth fighters.
timeline.intro_lede: From the first jet fighters of the Cold War to fifth-generation stealth aircraft — a chronicle of the planes that redefined air superiority.
timeline.outro_desc: The sixth generation is in development. NGAD, FCAS, Tempest…
timeline.no_aircraft: No aircraft with an operational date.
timeline.era_1940_desc2: The last generations of propeller aircraft rule the skies. The era of Mustangs, Spitfires and Zeros is ending — piston engines reach their technological limits just as the jet emerges.
timeline.era_1950_title2: The arrival of the jet engine
timeline.era_1950_desc2: Jet propulsion revolutionizes military aviation. MiG-15s and F-86 Sabres clash in Korean skies in the first ever jet-to-jet combats. The race to Mach begins.
timeline.era_1960_desc2: The era of overpowered interceptors. Mach 2 becomes the norm, air-to-air missiles progressively replace cannons, and doctrine favors speed and altitude over maneuverability.
timeline.era_1970_desc2: Vietnam lessons force a return to maneuverability and close combat. Birth of the 4th generation: F-14, F-15, F-16, MiG-29, Su-27 — machines designed to dominate across all flight regimes.
timeline.era_1980_desc2: Pulse-Doppler radars, BVR missiles and electronic countermeasures transform air combat. Stealth appears with the F-117 — a plane no one is supposed to see.
timeline.era_1990_desc2: The Gulf War demonstrates Western supremacy. Precision strikes, sensor fusion and electronic warfare redefine the rules. The 4.5 generation extends the life of existing fighters.
timeline.era_2000_desc2: The F-22 Raptor ushers in the fifth generation: stealth, supercruise, fusion avionics. Asymmetric conflicts and multi-role operations dominate. Air superiority is decided before visual contact.
timeline.era_2010_desc2: F-35, J-20, Su-57 — major powers deploy their 5th generation fighters. Combat drones, onboard AI and networked warfare reshape the aerial battlefield.
timeline.era_2020_desc2: NGAD, FCAS, Tempest: major nations prepare their 6th generation fighters. Loyal wingman drones, AI, directed energy weapons, active stealth — the future of air combat is being drawn now.
timeline.dossier_lede: Since Hiroshima, military aviation has never stopped redrawing the rules of power. Every decade has its takeoff, its crash, its doctrinal turn — and its machines that sometimes speak louder than any treaty.
timeline.era_1940_narrative: Even before Japan's surrender, the jet exists. In 1945, it is little more than an experiment — by 1949, it is the new language of air power. In four years, doctrines, armies and continents are rewritten at high speed. What begins in German labs ends on a North Korean tarmac.
timeline.era_1950_narrative: A decade later, the sky speaks two languages: American and Russian. The Korean War serves as a full-scale testing ground, the New Look doctrine turns the nuclear bomber into political currency, and Sputnik shifts aviation's ceiling to orbit. Between Mach 2 and space, only twenty-five kilometers of emptiness remain.
timeline.era_1960_narrative: The hottest decade of the Cold War. Cuba brings us to the edge; Vietnam teaches that air superiority is not enough if doctrine drifts. Above, the SR-71 Blackbird crosses Mach 3 as if air were no longer an obstacle. On the ground, SAMs learn to kill what used to be untouchable.
timeline.era_1970_narrative: After Vietnam, the West nurses its wounds and rebuilds. Variable geometry becomes the engineers' religion, European cooperation delivers its first fruit with the Tornado, and the SAMs of Yom Kippur remind everyone that high technology is not a shield. Electronic warfare grows into a theater of its own.
timeline.era_1980_narrative: The decade of high technology at war. Stealth walks out of black labs with the F-117 and the B-2, laser-guided precision guts Osirak, and British carriers resurrect at the Falklands. Then, on a November evening in 1989, a wall falls in Berlin — and the enemy for whom all these machines were drawn simply disappears.
timeline.era_1990_narrative: The sky becomes unipolar. Desert Storm delivers a global demonstration of absolute Western superiority, the USSR fades out, NATO bombs Serbia without a UN mandate. The F-22 Raptor lifts off. For ten years, the West stops doubting the sky — and Osama bin Laden prepares the counterstroke.
timeline.era_2000_narrative: 9/11 reopens everything. Afghanistan, Iraq, Lebanon, Georgia — military aviation becomes a permanent service, deployed everywhere, all the time. The Raptor goes on alert, the Rafale reaches maturity, and, quietly, Russia brings its Sukhois back home for a return match. The era of the empty sky is drawing to a close.
timeline.era_2010_narrative: China flies stealth, Russia bombs Syria, Turkish drones rewrite war in Nagorno-Karabakh, and Crimea flips in days without a single declaration. The F-35 enters service by the hundreds. For the first time since 1991, three large-scale air powers coexist — and watch each other.
timeline.era_2020_narrative: High-intensity war returns to Europe. In Ukraine, neither side manages to secure air superiority — a scenario judged impossible for thirty years. A drone kills Soleimani in Baghdad, Western F-16s enter Ukrainian service, and the NGAD, FCAS and Tempest programs frame the 2040s. The lone pilot is about to share the sky with his drones.

legal.pc_hero_subtitle: How we protect and use your personal data
legal.pc_intro_body: Vol d'Histoire is committed to protecting your privacy and personal data in accordance with the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR, EU 2016/679) and the French Data Protection Act.
legal.pc_sec1_body:
The data controller for personal data processing is:

Titouan Borde — personal project Vol d'Histoire

Email: vdh@titouan-borde.com
legal.pc_sec2_body:
2.1 Account data

When you create an account, we collect:

  • Name or pseudonym
  • Email address
  • Password (stored as a bcrypt hash, never in plain text)
  • Registration date and email verification status
  • Assigned role (user, editor or administrator)
  • Security data: failed login count, temporary lock, active sessions

2.2 Favorites

The aircraft you add to your favorites, linked to your account.

2.3 Contact form

First and last name (optional), email address, subject and message. The message is sent to us by email; it is not stored in the site's database. The server log keeps a record of the sending (sender address and subject).

2.4 Technical data

  • Server logs: IP address, browser, requested page, date and time
  • Technical error reports (Sentry)
  • On the sign-up, forgotten password and contact forms: technical data analysed by hCaptcha to tell humans from bots

2.5 Audience measurement (with your consent)

If you accept it, Google Analytics collects a pseudonymous browser identifier, the pages viewed and visit duration, the device and browser type, the referring page and an approximate location derived from the IP address.

2.6 Data stored in your browser

Language, hangar view, comparison tool, current filters and the guided tour already seen stay in your browser and are not sent to the server (see section 6).
legal.pc_sec3_body:
Your data is processed for the following purposes:

  • Account management (sign-up, login, email verification, password reset, favorites) — legal basis: performance of the contract (Terms of Use)
  • Service emails (verification, reset, email change) — legal basis: performance of the contract
  • Service security (attempt limiting, temporary lock, server logs, hCaptcha on sign-up, forgotten password and contact) — legal basis: legitimate interest
  • Answering your contact requests — legal basis: legitimate interest
  • Technical error tracking (Sentry) — legal basis: legitimate interest
  • Audience measurement (Google Analytics, pseudonymous data) — legal basis: consent

Your data is never used for advertising or profiling.
legal.pc_sec4_body:
• Account and favorites: until the account is deleted. Deletion, from your settings or on request, is immediate and permanent.
  • Account whose email was not verified: deleted automatically 7 days after sign-up.
  • Links sent by email: email verification 30 minutes, email change 30 minutes, password reset 15 minutes; each link can be used only once.
  • Access token: 15 minutes.
  • Session (refresh token): 7 days, revoked on logout and on password change. A revoked session stays in the database until it expires, to detect fraudulent reuse.
  • Lock after 10 failed logins: 15 minutes.
  • Contact requests: 12 months in the publisher's mailbox, then deleted.
  • Server logs: 12 months at most.
  • Error reports (Sentry): 30 days.
  • Audience measurement: Google Analytics cookies 13 months at most; data kept 14 months in Google Analytics.
  • Your cookie choice: 6 months, then you are asked again.
legal.pc_sec5_body:
Your personal data is never sold. It is disclosed to authorities only when legally required.

The following providers process some data on our behalf:

  • OVHcloud (OVH SAS, France) — hosting of the server and database, email delivery. Data hosted in France, within the European Union.
  • Google (Google Ireland Limited; Google LLC, United States) — Google Analytics and Google Tag Manager, only if you accept audience measurement.
  • Functional Software, Inc. (Sentry) (United States) — technical error reports, stored in Sentry's European Union region (Germany).
  • Intuition Machines, Inc. (hCaptcha) (United States) — bot protection on the sign-up, forgotten password and contact forms.

Transfers outside the European Union

Data processed by Google, Sentry and hCaptcha may be transferred to the United States. These transfers rely on the European Commission adequacy decision of 10 July 2023 (EU–US Data Privacy Framework): Google LLC, Functional Software, Inc. (Sentry) and Intuition Machines, Inc. (hCaptcha) are certified under it, with active participation checked on 10 November 2026 on the official list (dataprivacyframework.gov). For any question about these safeguards, write to vdh@titouan-borde.com.
legal.pc_sec7_body:
We implement technical and organizational measures to protect your data:

  • Encryption in transit: HTTPS on all connections, HSTS enabled
  • Security headers: Content-Security-Policy (CSP), X-Frame-Options, X-Content-Type-Options, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy
  • Passwords: bcrypt hashing with a unique salt, never stored in plain text. Policy: 8 to 128 characters, at least 1 uppercase, 1 lowercase and 1 digit
  • Sessions: short-lived signed tokens, sessions stored in the database and revocable, all sessions closed on password change
  • Rate limiting: protection of sensitive routes (sign-up, login, forgotten password, contact) against brute-force attacks
  • hCaptcha: bot protection on public forms
  • Parameterized SQL queries: protection against SQL injection
  • Backups of the database
  • Regular updates of dependencies and security patches

Despite these measures, no system is infallible. In the event of a personal data breach, we will notify the CNIL within 72 hours where it poses a risk to your rights (GDPR Article 33) and, if that risk is high, we will inform you without undue delay (Article 34).
legal.pc_sec8_body:
In accordance with the GDPR, you have the following rights:

  • Right of access — view the data we hold about you
  • Right of rectification — correct inaccurate or incomplete data
  • Right to erasure ("right to be forgotten")
  • Right to object to processing based on legitimate interest
  • Right to restrict processing
  • Right to data portability — retrieve your data in a machine-readable format
  • Right to withdraw consent at any time, for audience measurement

Exercising your rights

From your account, in your settings:

  • Profile — correct your name or email address
  • Cookies & Privacy › Download my data — JSON file with your profile and favorites (access and portability)
  • Danger Zone — delete your account, immediately and permanently

For any other right, or if you have no account, write to vdh@titouan-borde.com. We respond within one month. Proof of identity may be requested in case of reasonable doubt.

Complaint to the CNIL

If you believe your rights are not respected, you may file a complaint with the French Data Protection Authority (CNIL):

CNIL — 3 Place de Fontenoy, TSA 80715, 75334 PARIS CEDEX 07, France

Website: www.cnil.fr/en
legal.pc_sec9_body:
The minimum age to create an account on Vol d'Histoire is 15 years, in accordance with Article 8 of the GDPR as transposed into French law.

  • Minors under 15 may browse the site but cannot create an account without the consent of a parent or legal guardian
  • We do not knowingly collect personal data from children under 15
  • If you are a parent and notice that a minor has provided data without your consent, please contact us for immediate deletion
legal.pc_sec10_body:
This policy may change with the site or the regulations. The date of the last update is shown at the bottom of the page. In the event of a substantial change, we will inform you through a message on the site and, if you have an account, by email.

Version history

  • Version 2.0 — 10 November 2026: durations aligned with how the site actually works (immediate account deletion, 30- and 15-minute links), cookie choice kept 6 months, "preference" category removed, tracker inventory rewritten, contact form described, transfers outside the EU clarified, data download from the settings.
  • Version 1.1 — 8 September 2026: audience measurement relies on consent; session token durations corrected.
  • Version 1.0 — April 2026: first publication.
legal.pc_sec11_body:
For any questions about this policy or the processing of your data:

Data controller: Titouan Borde

2.2 Access requirements

legal.cgu_sec3_body:

After signing up, you receive an email with a verification link valid for 30 minutes, usable once. Your account must be verified before you can log in. If you forget your password, you can request a reset link from the "Forgot password" page, protected by hCaptcha. The link is valid for 15 minutes and can be used only once. For security reasons, we never confirm whether an account is associated with an email address.

Before deleting your account, you can download your data from Settings › Cookies & Privacy.

credits.hero_subtitle: Authors and licences of the catalogue photographs
credits.intro_body:
Most aircraft photographs come from Wikimedia Commons. Each one remains subject to its original licence: public domain, CC0 or Creative Commons licences that require crediting the author (BY) and, for some, sharing adaptations under the same licence (BY-SA).

All images have been modified for the site: resized, converted to WebP and AVIF and turned into thumbnails. The author and licence of each photo are also shown under the image, on the aircraft page. For part of the original catalogue, the author is not yet documented.

Found an attribution error, or an image of yours that you want removed? Write to vdh@titouan-borde.com.
